fictional_notice: FICTIONAL TEST DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Northstar Planner is an invented brand. Every name, product, price, policy, owner role, and fact in this pack is invented for software testing and describes no real company, product, or person. Do not publish this content or present it as real.

spec.purpose: A fictional, text-only evaluation dataset for checking a brand-guideline review tool against expected findings.
spec.evaluation_date_rule: All fact status, expiry, supersession, and offer tests use the fixed evaluation_as_of_date 2026-10-23. Test code must never read the system clock to decide whether a fact is active, expired, or superseded.

field_definitions.dataset_id: Stable identifier for this evaluation dataset.
field_definitions.guidelines_file: Repository-relative path to the guideline pack used for citations and expected IDs.
field_definitions.drafts_file: Repository-relative path to the draft source used for draft and revised-draft cases.
field_definitions.is_fictional: True when every brand, product, person, price, and policy in the dataset is invented.
field_definitions.fictional_notice: Plain-language notice that the dataset is fictional and must not be published as real.
field_definitions.evaluation_as_of_date: Fixed date used for all fact and offer status decisions.
field_definitions.spec: This object: field definitions, enums, matching rules, and metric definitions.
field_definitions.snippets: Array of 17 short inputs. Each snippet has id, channel, headline (string or null), and text. Expected findings live on test_cases, not here.
field_definitions.test_cases: Ordered array of 54 cases. IDs run from NS-TC-001 to NS-TC-054.
field_definitions.test_case.id: Unique test case ID, zero-padded to three digits.
field_definitions.test_case.case_type: One of the case_type enum values.
field_definitions.test_case.input: The input that must be run once.
field_definitions.test_case.input.type: One of draft, revised_draft, or snippet.
field_definitions.test_case.input.id: Draft ID for draft inputs, or snippet ID for snippet inputs.
field_definitions.test_case.input.text_source: For draft and revised_draft inputs: file, draft_id, and field. For snippet inputs: snippet_id. The runner loads the text from the source, never by retyping it.
field_definitions.test_case.target_finding_id: For draft-derived cases, the matching expected finding ID from sample-drafts.json. For snippet-derived cases, a synthetic ID of the form NS-SNIP-NN-FN. Null for no-finding cases.
field_definitions.test_case.expected: Expected result object for this case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.outcome: One of finding, no_finding, or needs_human_judgement.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.rule_or_fact_id: Primary expected rule or fact ID, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.acceptable_alternate_: Alternate guideline IDs that also count as a correct citation for this case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.finding_type: Plain finding-type label, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.span_text: Exact expected span, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.start: Inclusive Unicode code-point offset of the expected span, or null.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.end: Exclusive Unicode code-point offset of the expected span, or null.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.expected_finding: One plain sentence describing the expected finding, or null.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.citation: Source document ID and section, looked up from the guidelines file for the primary expected ID, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.severity: One of low, medium, or high, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.label: Expected label enum value, or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.suggested_fix: Expected suggested fix copied from source for draft cases or written for snippet cases, or null.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.human_review_required: Boolean or null for a no-finding case.
field_definitions.test_case.expected.acceptable_alternativ: Optional list of other acceptable outcomes. Each item has outcome, rule_or_fact_id, and reason. Only snippet 01 uses this field, for needs_human_judgement on NS-NAME-001.
field_definitions.test_case.notes: Short plain-language note for the runner or reviewer.
field_definitions.coverage: Computed lists of guideline IDs that appear in at least one test case, with counts per case_type. Counts include primary IDs, acceptable alternates, and acceptable alternative outcomes.
field_definitions.known_coverage_gaps: Computed list of rule and fact IDs not covered by any positive case, each with an honest reason.
field_definitions.results_template: One empty record per test case. Every field is null except test_case_id and the status value not_run.

matching_rules.summary: A returned finding matches an expected finding only when the cited ID, span overlap, and one-to-one conditions all hold.
conditions: The returned finding's cited ID equals expected.rule_or_fact_id or appears in expected.acceptable_alternate_ids.

The returned finding's span overlaps the expected span by at least 50% of the expected span's characters. Overlap is max(0, min(returned_end, expected_end) - max(returned_start, expected_start)); the threshold is 0.5 * (expected_end - expected_start).

Matching is one-to-one: each returned finding may match at most one expected finding, and each expected finding may be matched by at most one returned finding. Use an assignment that maximizes valid matches and break ties deterministically.
Returned findings that match nothing are false positives, including extra findings on negative or edge inputs.
matching_rules.proposal_note: These matching rules are a proposal. Confirm them against docs/api-contracts.md before relying on any score.

metrics.name: Finding precision
metrics.formula_words: True positives divided by true positives plus false positives.
metrics.what_is_counted: TP is returned findings matched one-to-one to an expected finding. FP is returned findings that match no expected finding, including any finding raised on a negative or edge input.
metrics.breakdowns: Overall; by the cited rule or fact category from the guidelines file; and by check_method (computed, ai, hybrid).

metrics.name: Finding recall
metrics.formula_words: True positives divided by true positives plus false negatives.
metrics.what_is_counted: TP is returned findings matched one-to-one to an expected finding. FN is expected findings with no match.
metrics.breakdowns: Overall; by the cited rule or fact category from the guidelines file; and by check_method (computed, ai, hybrid).

metrics.name: Finding F1
metrics.formula_words: Two times precision times recall, divided by precision plus recall.
metrics.what_is_counted: P is finding precision and R is finding recall. Report the same overall, category, and check_method breakdowns as precision and recall.
metrics.breakdowns: Overall; by the cited rule or fact category from the guidelines file; and by check_method (computed, ai, hybrid).

metrics.name: Citation validity rate
metrics.formula_words: Returned findings whose cited ID exists in the guidelines file and whose cited text a human reviewer judges to support the finding, divided by all returned findings.
metrics.what_is_counted: ID_exists is 1 when the cited ID is present in the guidelines file. Human_support is 1 when a reviewer judges the cited text to support the finding, otherwise 0. Score both parts for every returned finding. Report the automated part separately from the human-judged part.

components.name: Automated ID-exists rate
components.formula_words: Returned findings whose cited ID exists in the guidelines file divided by all returned findings.
components.what_is_counted: The automated check only; it does not judge whether the cited text supports the finding.

components.name: Human-judged citation support rate
components.formula_words: Returned findings whose cited text a human reviewer judges to support the finding divided by all returned findings.
components.what_is_counted: The reviewer scores support as 0 or 1 for each returned finding.

metrics.notes: 100% is the plan's target, not a result. Report the automated and human parts separately.

metrics.name: Correct severity rate
metrics.formula_words: Among true-positive findings, the share whose returned severity equals the expected severity.
metrics.what_is_counted: Only findings already matched as true positives are scored.

components.name: Severity within one level
components.formula_words: Among true-positive findings, the share whose returned severity is within one level of the expected severity.
components.what_is_counted: Severity order is low < medium < high. One level means the same level or an adjacent level.

metrics.name: Suggested-fix usefulness
metrics.formula_words: Sum of reviewer usefulness scores divided by two times the number of true-positive findings.
metrics.what_is_counted: Each true-positive finding receives a reviewer score: 0 = missing, wrong, or changes the meaning; 1 = points in the right direction but incomplete; 2 = usable as written, fixes the issue, keeps the creator's meaning, and introduces no new violation.

components.name: Fix re-check pass rate
components.formula_words: Share of true-positive fixes that, once applied, raise no finding for the same rule.
components.what_is_counted: Automated re-check of the applied fix for the same rule only.

metrics.name: False-positive rate on compliant inputs
metrics.formula_words: Number of compliant inputs with at least one returned finding divided by the number of compliant inputs.
metrics.what_is_counted: Compliant inputs are the negative and edge test cases. A near-expiry notice to a fact owner is not a finding.

components.name: Returned findings per compliant input
components.formula_words: Total returned findings on compliant inputs divided by the number of compliant inputs.
components.what_is_counted: All returned findings on negative and edge inputs, including duplicate rule hits.

metrics.name: Ambiguity handling rate
metrics.formula_words: Among ambiguous cases, the share where the tool returns needs_human_judgement or an explicitly low confidence instead of a confident violation.
metrics.what_is_counted: Ambiguous cases are the test cases with case_type ambiguous.

metrics.name: High-severity recall
metrics.formula_words: Recall computed over expected findings whose severity is high.
metrics.what_is_counted: Only expected findings with severity high are included in the denominator and numerator.

spec.metrics_note: No scores have been measured. All results fields stay null until the tests are actually run.
